rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is the speaker addressing the believers with him; the phrase about his Lord's forgiveness signals this attribution.
rows.anchor: أي نوح عليه السلام لمن معه من المؤمنين كما ينبيء عنه قوله تعالى : ( إن ربي لغفور رحيم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A view makes God the speaker, but al-Alusi objects that the wording would then naturally be my Lord, not your Lord.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الضمير لله تعالى وفيه أنه لو كان كذلك لكان المناسب إن ربكم إلخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He suggests Noah said this after loading the pairs that he had been commanded to carry into the Ark.
rows.anchor: ولعل هذا القول بعد إدخال ما أمر بحمله في الفلك من الأزواج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ride means enter or settle in the Ark; calling it riding compares the vessel on water to a mount on land, a derived metaphor.
rows.anchor: أي صيروا فيها وجعل ذلك ركوبا لأنها في الماء كالمركوب في الأرض ففيه استعارة تبعية

rows.speaker: القاضي البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Baydawi treats the expression as an implicit metaphor, with the preposition marking the transition into the vessel.
rows.anchor: وقيل : استعارة مكنية والتعدية بفي لاعتبار الصيرورة وإلا فالفعل يتعدى بنفسه وإلى هذا ذهب القاضي البيضاوي

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another explanation says the preposition fi is used because the verb includes the sense of entering.
rows.anchor: وقيل : التعدية بذلك لأنه ضمن معنى إدخلوا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another explanation supplies water as the object: ride the water in the Ark.
rows.anchor: وقيل : تقديره اركبوا الماء فيها

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A further view treats fi as an emphatic extra preposition.
rows.anchor: وقيل : في زائدة للتوكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says the first explanation of the preposition is the most apt.
rows.anchor: وكأن الأول أولى

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: A riding verb applied to a moving object takes fi to preserve its locative sense; this does not mean the passengers were inside, since reports place them above.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المحققين : الركوب العلو على شيء متحرك ويتعدى بنفسه وإستعماله بفي ليس لأن المأمور به كونهم في جوفها لا فوقها كما ظن

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: Riding means mounting something moving, voluntarily like an animal or by force like a ship; the verb is direct with animals but takes fi with ships.
rows.anchor: معنى الركوب العلو على شيء له حركة إما إرادية كالحيوان أو قسرية كالسفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading is literal riding here, although some explicitly say the usage is not literal.
rows.anchor: وظاهره أن الركوب ههنا حقيقي وصرح بعضهم أنه ليس به

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says riding originally means being on an animal's back, though it is also used for ships.
rows.anchor: وقال الراغب : الركوب في الأصل كون الإنسان على ظهر حيوان وقد يستعمل في السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bismi llah is a circumstantial phrase attached to the subject of ride; its bāʾ marks accompaniment, meaning they ride while naming God.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت ملابسة إسم الله عز إسمه بذكره قالوا : المعنى إركبوا مسمين الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, an omitted circumstantial phrase is supplied: ride while saying bismi llah, with the quoted phrase standing in its place.
rows.anchor: وجوزوا أن تكون الحال محذوفة وهذا معمول لها ساد مسدها ولذلك سموه حالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Majraha and mursaha may be temporal accusatives, as verbal nouns or time-nouns, with an omitted waqt understood as in the example about the star's setting.
rows.anchor: نصب على الظرفية أي وقت إجرائها وإرسائها على أنهما إسما زمان أو مصدران ميميان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may instead be place-nouns governed by the locative phrase or by saying; they cannot sensibly be governed by ride, whose command is to seek blessing or say God's name there.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكونا غسمي مكان وإنتصابهما بالإستقرار الذي تعلق به الجار والمجرور أو بقائلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some object to the accusative because a delimited place normally requires fi, while others allow it because the expression remains semantically open.
rows.anchor: وتعقب القول بانتصابهما مطلقا بأنهما محدودان ومحدود المكان لابد له من في وبعضهم يجوز النصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nominative parsing is also proposed: the two forms can be subjects governed by the adverb, or coordinated subjects with bismi llah as predicate and an omitted predicate understood.
rows.anchor: وجوز رفعهما فاعلين بالظرف لإعتماده على ذي الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence can resume the discourse: Noah first orders boarding, then assures them that sailing and landing occur by God's name, encouraging them and easing fear of drowning.
rows.anchor: والجملة إما مقتضية منقطعة عما قبلها لإختلافهما خبرا وطلبا على أن نوحا عليه السلام أمرهم بالركوب

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak reports that Noah said bismi llah when setting the Ark in motion and again when bringing it to rest.
rows.anchor: ويروى عن الضحاك أنه عليه السلام كان إذا أراد أن يجريها يقول ( بسم الله ) فتجري وإذا أراد أن يرسيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is a prospective circumstantial clause describing the Ark as sailing and settling by God's name.
rows.anchor: وهي حال مقدرة إذ لا إجراء ولا إرساء وقت الركوب كذا قيل

rows.speaker: التقريب
rows.claim: Al-Taqrib objects that a clause cannot be a prospective circumstantial phrase: the wording implies sailing by God's name occurs while they board.
rows.anchor: وتعقبه في التقريب بأن الحال إنما تكون مقدرة إذا كانت مفردة كمجراة أما إذا كانت جملة فلا

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf answers that a clause can be prospective too, comparing it with entering Paradise while destined to remain there.
rows.anchor: وأجاب عنه في الكشف بأنه لا فرق بين قوله تعالى : ( ادخلوها خالدين )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says the response misses al-Taqrib's point: a clause implies realized, continuing involvement, so a pending event is awkward when a single-word circumstantial phrase is available.
rows.anchor: فإنهم ذكروا أن الفرق بين الحال إذا كانت مفردة وإذا كانت جملة أن الثانية تقتضي التحقق في نفسها والتلبس بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the phrase a prospective circumstantial clause of the riders is challenged because it lacks a link to them and requires a strained nominal paraphrase.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن تكون حالا مقدرة أيضا من فاعل ( اركبوا ) واعترض بأنه لا عائد على ذي الحال

rows.speaker: الرضي
rows.claim: Al-Radi allows a nominal circumstantial clause to lack both usual links when the relation of accompaniment is obvious.
rows.anchor: والقول بأن الرضي قد ذكر أن الجملة الحالية إذا كانت اسمية قد تخلو من الرابطين عند ظهور الملابسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says the appeal to al-Radi is unsound here, and rejects as overbroad the rules that nominal circumstantials must always have waw and that prospective circumstantials cannot be clauses.
rows.anchor: نعم كون الإسمية لابد فيها من الواو والقول بأن الحال المقدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further parsing treats the word name as an inserted element, as in Labid's line; by God then means by His power, command, or permission, with metaphorical attribution.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون الإسم مقحما كما في قول لبيد : فقوما وقولا بالذي قد عرفتما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce majraha and mursaha with an open mīm as verbal nouns, time-nouns, or place-nouns from the triliteral verbs jara and rasa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجراها ومرساها بفتح الميم مصدرين أو زمانين أو مكانين على أنهما من جرى ورسا الثلاثيين

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reads the forms as active participles, mujriha and mursiha.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد مجريها ومرسيها بصيغة اسم الفاعل

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqaʾ parses Mujahid's forms as adjectives modifying the divine name.
rows.anchor: وخرج ذلك أبو البقاء على أنهما صفتان للاسم الجليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adjective analysis is challenged because a future active participle has a non-definite annexation and cannot modify a definite noun; badal is the sounder parsing.
rows.anchor: إن إضافة اسم الفاعل إذا كان بمعنى المستقبل لفظية فهو نكرة لا يصح توصيف المعرفة به فالحق البدلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the adjective a semantic rather than syntactic description is judged a far-fetched response to the objection.
rows.anchor: والقول بأن مراد المعرب الصفة المعنوية لا النعت النحوي فلا ينافي البدلية بعيد

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil allows a normally incomplete annexation to become complete and definite, except for the annexation of an adjective of inherent quality.
rows.anchor: لكن عن الخليل أن ما كانت إضافته غير محضة قد يصح أن تجعل محضة فتعرف إلا ما كان من الصفة المشبهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rusu means firmness and stability; an unnamed poet's line uses it of a steadfast soul when the coward's soul is unsettled.
rows.anchor: والرسو الثبوت والإستقرار ومنه قول الشاعر : فصبرت نفسا عند ذلك حرة ( ترسو ) إذا نفس الجبان تطلع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing clause explains why they were saved: without God's forgiveness and mercy, their faith would not merit rescue from the calamity, which accords with Sunni teaching that rescue is sheer grace.
rows.anchor: وفيه دلالة على أن نجاتهم لم تكن عن استحقاق بسبب أنهم كانوا مؤمنين بل بمحض رحمة الله تعالى وغفرانه على ما عليه أهل السنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing clause cannot directly justify the order to board because the required causal relation is absent unless an unstated rationale is supplied.
rows.anchor: ومنع صلاحية كونها علة لاركبوا لعدم المناسبة فيقدر ما يصح به الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One supplied rationale is: obey this command so God may save you through forgiveness and mercy; another is to invoke God and fear no drowning because He is forgiving and merciful.
rows.anchor: بأن يقال : متثلوا هذا الحكم لينجيكم من الهلاك بمغفرته ورحمته

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some make the clause a reason for boarding because it alludes to the passengers' eventual salvation.
rows.anchor: وجعلها بعضهم تعليلا بالنظر إلى ما فيها من الإشارة إلى النجاة فكأنه قيل : اركبوا لينجيكم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah was revealed after Pharaoh and his people had perished, so it could guide the Israelites thereafter; Pharaoh's people had instead been commanded to worship God, abandon Pharaoh's monstrous claim, and free Israel from captivity.
rows.anchor: فإن نزولها إنما كان بعد مهلك فرعون وقومه قاطبة ليعمل بها بنوا إسرائيل فيما يأتون ويذرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This chronology makes it problematic to count the crop and life losses, or the mountain's shading, among the nine signs sent to Pharaoh; they occurred later. Replacing them with the sea's parting and cloud shade does not solve the timing problem for the latter.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا يعلم ما في عد النقص من الثمرات والنقص من الأنفس آية واحدة من الآيات التسع وعد إظلال الجبل منها

rows.speaker: بعض الأفاضل
rows.claim: One answer attaches the phrase to the unqualified sending of Moses, rather than to the sending specifically with the Torah.
rows.anchor: أما أولا فبما صرحوا به من جواز إرجاع الضمير وتعلق الجار ونحوه بالمطلق الذي في ضمن المقيد

rows.speaker: بعض الأفاضل
rows.claim: A second answer says Moses was sent to Israel as well as Pharaoh and takes Pharaoh's elite broadly enough to include Israel, distributing the signs between them.
rows.anchor: وأما ثانيا فبأن يقال : إن موسى عليه السلام كما أرسل إلى الفراعنة أرسل إلى بني إسرائيل أيضا

rows.speaker: الحافظ الطاشكندي
rows.claim: Al-Tashkandi raised the objection about counting the Torah among the signs in Moses' mission to Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: وفي مجموعة سري الدين المصري أن هذا السؤال مما أورد الحافظ الطاشكندي على مخدوم الملك

rows.speaker: مخدوم الملك
rows.claim: One response makes bā-āyātinā a prospective circumstantial phrase, so the mission is described as accompanied by signs even if some appeared after Pharaoh's death.
rows.anchor: فأجاب بأن قوله سبحانه : ( بآياتنا ) حال مقدرة أي مقدرين تلبسه أو نصرته بالآيات والسلطان

rows.speaker: مخدوم الملك
rows.claim: Another response says revelation of the Torah began in Pharaoh's lifetime, though its complete written form was given after the drowning; earlier tablets were wood, while the complete tablets were said to be emerald, ruby, or hard stone.
rows.anchor: وبأنه قيل : إن إعطاءه التوراة مجموعا مرتبا مكتوبا في الألواح بعد غرق فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi finds the prospective-circumstantial answer unacceptable to sound literary judgment and says the account of the Torah's timing lacks sound reports.
rows.anchor: ولا يخفى أن الذهاب إلى كون الحال مقدرة مما لا يكاد يقبله الذوق السليم وما حكى من إعطاء التوراة مجموعا كان بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects both the unrestricted-sending and Israel-included-among-Pharaoh's-elite answers as improper interpretations of revelation; the elite cannot include Israel when they are attached to Pharaoh and destined for the Fire.
rows.anchor: وما ذكر أولا من حديث التعلق بالمطلق وثانيا من حمل ( الملأ ) على ما يشمل بني إسرائيل الخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attaching ila Firʿawn to the clear authority, literally or by implication, with an understood authority sent to Pharaoh, is proposed as possible, though Al-Alusi says it has an evident difficulty.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لو جعل ( إلى فرعون ) متعلقا ( بسلطان مبين ) لفظا أو معنى على تقدير وسلطان مرسل به إلى فرعون لم يبعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elite are singled out although Moses was sent to everyone because they led deliberation and governance, while others followed their lead.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص الملأ مع عموم رسالة موسى عليه السلام للقوم كافة لأصالتهم في الرأي وتدبير الأمور واتباع الغير لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text leaves Pharaoh's disbelief and persistence implicit because these were obvious; it instead highlights the elite's choice between Moses' guidance and Pharaoh's misguidance and censures their choice.
rows.anchor: ولم يصرح بكفر فرعون بالآيات وانهماكه فيما كان عليه من الضلال والإضلال بل اقتصر على ذكر شأن ملائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ in they followed signals their sudden response and Pharaoh's haste to disbelieve and command disbelief, with virtually no delay after the message.
rows.anchor: وإيراد الفاء للإشعار بمفاجأتهم في الإتباع ومسارعة فرعون إلى الكفر والأمر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes Pharaoh's affair as his way or course and reads they followed as continuing their prior adherence, like someone admonished but not deterred.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يراد من الأمر الطريقة والشأن قيل : ومعنى ( فاتبعوا ) فاستمروا على الإتباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another alternative reads the phrase as adopting Pharaoh's newly expressed disbelief in Moses; the fāʾ marks their immediate conformity after the message, not conduct predating Pharaoh's rejection.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد فاتصفوا بما اتصف به فرعون من الكفر بما جاء به موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says there is no need to force the continuation reading or make the fāʾ work as in the example of rebuking someone and his being deterred.
rows.anchor: فلا ضرورة إلى الحمل على الإستمرار وجعل الفاء كما في قولك : زجرته فأنزجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording repeats Pharaoh's name instead of using a pronoun so readers do not mistake the referent for Moses and so the followers' choice of a corrupt, misguided leader is more sharply censured.
rows.anchor: وعدل عن أمره إلى أمر فرعون لدفع توهم رجوع الضمير إلى موسى عليه السلام من أول الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barashid means rightly guided or possessing right guidance, the opposite of error; attributing that quality to Pharaoh's command is figurative and heightens regret over the good they lost in both worlds.
rows.anchor: أي براشد أو بذي رشد والرشد ضد الغي وإسناده إلى الأمر مجازي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, rushd is a metonym for praiseworthiness and the attribution is literal: Pharaoh's command was not good or praiseworthy in outcome.
rows.anchor: أي وما أمر فرعون بصالح حميد العاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first interpretation of Pharaoh's command, the statement about leading his people to the Fire independently answers an implicit question about the fate of leader and followers.
rows.anchor: على الأول استئناف وقع جوابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the second interpretation, the statement explains why Pharaoh's course has no sound outcome.
rows.anchor: وعلى الثاني تفسير وإيضاح لعدم صلاح عاقبته

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: The clause saying Pharaoh's command was not rightly guided can be a circumstantial phrase attached either to the followers or to the command they followed; al-Zamakhshari prefers attachment to the object.
rows.anchor: وجملة ( وما أمر ) الخ جواز أن تكون حالا من فاعل اتبعوا وأن تكون حالا من مفعوله قيل : وهو مختار الزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's people here includes both his elite and the rest of his population.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالقوم ما يشمل الملأ وغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaqdumu means to go ahead or lead, as related forms for a caravan's front, an army's vanguard, and the front of the eye also indicate.
rows.anchor: و ( يقدم ) كينصر من قدم كنصر بمعنى تقدم ومنه قادمة الرحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past-tense فأوردهم means he will bring them to the Fire; the past form signals that the event is certain to occur.
rows.anchor: والمراد من أوردهم يوردهم والتعبير به دونه للإيذان بتحقق وقوعه لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that he brought them to a worldly fire, meaning the disbelief that causes it, is unsound.
rows.anchor: والقول : بأنه باق على حقيقته والمراد فأوردهم في الدنيا النار أي موجبها وهو الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fire is a second object of bring; it is an ironic implicit metaphor for the opposite, water, and on a figurative reading bringing itself means driving them to the Fire.
rows.anchor: ونصب النار على أنه مفعول ثان لأوردهم وهي استعارة مكنية تهكمية للضد وهو الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Pharaoh is implicitly likened to a water scout who goes ahead, while his followers are imagined as the incoming water; the whole scene may instead be a parable.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يقال : إنه شبه فرعون بالفارط وهو الذي يتقدم القوم للماء

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some make yaqdam and awrada compete to govern Fire, with the second verb used and the first verb's object omitted; al-Alusi finds this weak.
rows.anchor: وجوز بعضهم كون ( يقدم ) وأورد متنازعين في النار إلا أنه أعمل الثاني وحذف مفعول الأول وليس بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water image in ward is a drink brought to quench thirst and cool hearts, whereas Fire tears hearts apart and burns them; the disparaged object is implicitly Fire.
rows.anchor: أي بئس الورد الذي يردونه النار لأن الورد إنما يورد لتسكين العطش وتبريد الأكباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This parsing is criticized because the subject of biʾsa and its specified object do not agree, and because grammarians dispute whether the subject of praise or blame can be described.
rows.anchor: وتعقب بأنه لا بد من تصادق فاعل ( بئي ) ومخصوصها ولا تصادق على هذا

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya makes mawroud an adjective and Fire the specified object by ellipsis: the Fire is the wretched place of arrival.
rows.anchor: وجوز ابن عطية كون ( المورود ) صفة والمخصوص النار إلا أنه جعل الكلام على حذف المضاف

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another parses mawroud as the specified object itself, with an omitted annexed noun: the Fire is the wretched place of arrival.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من يجعل ( المورود ) هو المخصوص بالذم والمراد به النار ويقدر المضاف

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another makes ward the subject of blame meaning the arriving group, mawroud their adjective, and an omitted pronoun the specified object, so the people rather than the destination are blamed.
rows.anchor: ومن يجعل الورد فاعل ( بئس ) ويفسره بالجمع الوارد و ( المورود ) صفة لهم والمخصوص بالذم ضميرهم المحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows every unseen thing in the heavens and earth, and no one besides Him knows all of it.
rows.anchor: أي أنه سبحانه يعلم كل ما غاب في السموات والأرض ولا يعلم ذلك أحد سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every affair returns to God, so the Prophet's and his opponents' affairs inevitably return to Him.
rows.anchor: فيرجع لا محالة أمرك وأمرهم إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most of the seven canonical readers read yarjiʿ in the active voice; worship and reliance follow because God alone is the final resort and suffices.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أكثر السبعة ( يرجع ) بالبناء للفاعل من رجع رجوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ orders worship and reliance as consequences of all affairs returning to God; another explanation also grounds them in God's knowledge of every unseen thing.
rows.anchor: والفاء لترتيب الأمر بالعبادة والتوكل على كون مرجع الأمور كلها إليه وقيل : على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting reliance after worship indicates that reliance does not benefit without worship, since the order suggests precedence in rank or occurrence.
rows.anchor: وفي تأخير الأمر بالتوكل عن الأمر بالعبادة تنبيه على أن التوكل لا ينفع دونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, worship means obeying all commands, including guidance and proclamation, while reliance means trusting God in that work; continue preaching without distress over unbelievers.
rows.anchor: ومن التوكل التوكل فيه كأنه قيل : إمتثل ما أمرت به ودوام على الدعوة والتبليغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafi, Abu Amir, Hafs, Qatada, al-Aʿraj, Shayba, Abu Jaʿfar, and al-Jahdari read with tāʾ, addressing the Prophet and, by predominance, including the others; God recompenses each according to desert.
rows.anchor: بتاء الخطاب على تغليب المخاطب وبذلك قرأ نافع وأبو عامر وحفص وقتادة والأعرج وشيبة وأبو جعفر والجحدري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rest of the seven readers use yāʾ for third-person address, which is straightforward.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون من السبعة بالياء على الغيبة وذلك ظاهر

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb reports that the Torah opens with the opening of al-Anʿam and closes with Hud's final passage, beginning with God's ownership of the unseen.
rows.anchor: وفي زوائد الزهد لعبدالله بن أحمد بن حنبل وفضائل القرآن لابن الضريس عن كعب أن فاتحة التوراة فاتحة الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the allusive reading, the wretched and blessed are people wholly wretched and wholly blessed.
rows.anchor: يوم يأت لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه فمنهم شقي ) كامل الشقاوة ومنهم سعيد كامل السعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire of the wretched is deprivation from what they sought and the pains of their sins, a punishment of the soul.
rows.anchor: فأما الذين شقوا ففي النار ) أي نار الحرمان عن المراد وآلام ما اكتسبوه من الآثام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception from abiding in Fire leads the wretched to worse fires of the heart, through wrath and humiliation, and of the spirit, through veiling, curse, and subjugation.
rows.anchor: فيخرجون من ذلك إلى ما هو أشد منه من نيران القلب وذلك بالسخط والإذلال ونيران الروح وذلك بالحجب واللعن والقهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's being active in whatever He wills means no constraint or restriction can be imposed on Him.
rows.anchor: إن ربك فعال لما يريد ) لا حجر عليه سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Garden of the blessed is the Garden of fulfilled desires and pleasures, the garden of the soul.
rows.anchor: وأما الذين سعدوا ففي الجنة ) أي جنة حصول المراد واللذات وهي جنة النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessed rise by God's will to higher gardens of the heart through witnessing the attributes, and of the spirit through vision, beyond anything the senses or imagination conceive.
rows.anchor: فيخرجون من ذلك إلى ما هو أعلى وأعلى من جنات القلب في مقام تجليات الصفات وجنات الروح في مقام الشهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tanwin may mark a type, and the exception may mean a wretched person leaves Fire for Paradise by purifying the soul of what blocked the way.
rows.anchor: وقد يحمل التنوين على النوعية ويؤول الاستثناء بخروج الشقي من النار بالترقي من مقامه إلى الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stand firm by fulfilling God's and creatures' rights: guard His rights, honor His commands, and guide creation, while seeing multiplicity in unity and unity in multiplicity without neglecting reverence.
rows.anchor: أي في القيام بحقوق الحق والخلق وذلك بالمحافظة على حقوقه تعالى والتعظيم لأمره والتسديد لخلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who repent with the Prophet are monotheists who leave selfhood and their sense of independent existence for the station of abiding after annihilation.
rows.anchor: ومن تاب ) عن إنيته وذهب وجوده ( معك من المؤمنين ) الموحدين إلى مقام البقاء بعد الفناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says the Prophet's commanded steadfastness exceeds that of his companions; conjunction requires only sharing in the general act, not equal rank.
rows.anchor: إن الاستقامة المأمور بها صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم فوق الاستقامة المأمور بها من معه عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Junayd distinguishes steadfastness with fear and hope for worshipers, with awe and hope for the near ones, and without seeing one's own steadfastness for the gnostics.
rows.anchor: قال الجنيد قدس سره : الإستقامة مع الخوف والرجاء حال العابدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not transgress means do not leave the limits set by sacred law; leaving them is heresy.
rows.anchor: ولا تطغوا ) ولا تخرجوا عما حد لكم من الشريعة فإن الخروج عنها زندقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rukn means to incline even slightly toward those who do wrong.
rows.anchor: ولا تركنوا ) أي لا تميلوا أدنى ميل ( إلى الذين ظلموا ) وهي النفوس المظلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An allusive interpretation identifies the wrongdoers with darkened souls that are innately inclined to evil.
rows.anchor: وهي النفوس المظلمة المائلة إلى الشرور في أصل الخلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A saying about injustice being a trait of souls, except when another cause restrains them, is attributed in a report to Ali al-Rida through his father and Jaʿfar.
rows.anchor: كما قيل : الظلم من شيم النفوس فإن تجد ذا عفة فلعلة لم يظلم وروي ذلك عن علي بن موسى الرضا عن أبيه عن جعفر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another interpretation forbids following hypocrites, ignorant people, and bad companions.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المعنى لا تقتدوا بالمرائين والجاهلين وقرناء السوء

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A further interpretation forbids keeping company with evil people or sitting with innovators.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لا تصحبوا الأشرار ولا تجالسوا أهل البدع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to establish the prescribed prayer at its known times; prayer is the believer's ascent, as reports attest its lofty rank.
rows.anchor: أمر بإقامة الصلاة المفروضة على ما علمت وقد ذكروا أن الصلاة معراج المؤمن وفي الأخبار ما يدل على علو شأنها

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti says the lights of acts of obedience remove the darkness of acts of disobedience.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي : أنوار الطاعات تذهب بظلم المعاصي

rows.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Muʿadh says God covers a believer's sin, then forgives it, then replaces it with good deeds, citing 25:70.
rows.anchor: وقال يحيى بن معاذ : إن الله سبحانه لم يرض للمؤمن بالذنب حتى ستر ولم يرض بالستر حتى غفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer at the stated times and good deeds erasing wrongs remind those who remember God of presence, purity, gatheredness, intimacy, and spiritual taste.
rows.anchor: ذكرى للذاكرين تذكير لمن يذكر حاله عند الحضور مع الله تعالى في الصفاء والجمعية والأنس والذوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Be patient through God in steadfastness and with God in prayerful presence, without leaning toward anything else.
rows.anchor: واصبر ) بالله سبحانه في الإستقامة ومع الله تعالى بالحضور في الصلاة وعدم الركون إلى الغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The benefactors whose reward God does not waste are those who witness Him while fulfilling their duties.
rows.anchor: إن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين ) الذين يشاهدونه في حال القيام بالحقوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse urges commanding right and forbidding wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: فلو لا كان من القرون من قبلكم أو لو بقية ينهون عن الفساد في الأرض ) فيه حض على الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In an allusive reading, the towns are hearts and their inhabitants are the faculties.
rows.anchor: القرى فيه إشارة إلى القلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God willed, He could make people one community, equal in capacity and united in the religion of monotheism.
rows.anchor: ولو شاء ربك لجعل الناس أمة واحدة ) متساوية في الاستعداد متفقة على دين التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their continuing differences are differences of orientation and spiritual capacity.
rows.anchor: ولا يزالون مختلفين ) في الوجهة والأستعداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those shown mercy receive guidance to monotheism and divine enabling toward perfection; they agree in doctrine and aim and share a way, though their expressions differ.
rows.anchor: إلا من رحم ربك ) بهدايته إلى التوحيد وتوفيقه للكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted poem captures the unity beneath varied expressions: descriptions differ while the beauty they point toward is one.
rows.anchor: كما قيل : عباراتنا شتى وحسنك واحد وكل إلى ذاك الجمال يشير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created people for this difference so they could manifest His beauty, majesty, gentleness, and overpowering force.
rows.anchor: ولذلك ) الإختلاف ( خلقهم ) وذلك ليكونوا مظاهر جماله وجلاله ولطفه وقهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says difference completes the world's order and sustains earthly life.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ليتم نظام العالم ويحصل قوام الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The decree to fill Hell is completed and made firm because Hell is a rank of existence that wisdom does not leave unrealized while it remains possible.
rows.anchor: وتمت كلمة ربك ) أي أحكمت وأبرمت ( لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accounts of the messengers' trials, patience, and the destruction of their enemies strengthen the Prophet's heart.
rows.anchor: وكلا نقص عليك من أنباء الرسل ما نثبت به فؤادك ) لما اشتملت عليه من مقاساتهم الشدائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truth brought in this sura is not something one may turn away from; its admonition and reminder benefit believers.
rows.anchor: وجاءك في هذه ) السورة ( الحق ) الذي لا ينبغي المحيد عنه ( وموعظة وذكرى للمؤمنين )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This sura may be singled out for honor, though the whole Qur'an has this quality; each group draws from it according to its spiritual disposition, from outward meaning to inward vision of divine manifestation.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص هذه السورة بالذكر كما أشرنا إليه وقيل : للتشريف وإلا فالقرآن كله كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's unseen in the heavens and earth encompasses their diverse meanings.
rows.anchor: ولله غيب السموات ) على اختلاف معانيها ( والأرض ) كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every affair returns to God because the whole of every affair comes from Him.
rows.anchor: وإليه يرجع الأمر كله ) أي كل شأن من الشئون فإن الكل منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship means setting aside self-interest and adhering to God's command with proper adab.
rows.anchor: فاعبده ) أسقط عنك حظوظ نفسك وقف مع الأمر بشرط الأدب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trust God without worrying over what He has already taken care of; attend to what He has commanded you to do.
rows.anchor: وتوكل عليه ) لا تهتم بما قد كفيته واهتم بما ندبت إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not heedless of people's deeds and recompenses each according to what wisdom requires.
rows.anchor: وما ربك بغافل عما تعملون ) فيجازي كلا حسبما تقتضيه الحكمة
